identity.name: Kingdom of the Isles
alt_names: Kingdom of Mann and the Isles

land.text: the Hebrides and the Isle of Man, which the 1266 Treaty of Perth 'yielded' to Scotland; Cliopatria's Alba shape grows to include them in 1272

successors.note: Cliopatria's Kingdom of Alba row (900-1293) has the Isles' cells from its 1272 shape (25 of the 36 cells of the 1094 Isles shape), six years after the treaty.

capitals.name: Isle of Man (seat not named on the page)
capitals.note: The page names no capital in its infobox or body; the coordinates are the centroid of the island, where Godred Crovan began in 1079 and Magnus Olafsson was the last king in 1265. The kings also held the Hebrides and, for Godred Crovan, Dublin.

correction.text: the Isle of Man, taken by Godred Crovan from Fingal in 1079

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first Kingdom of the Isles shape begins in 1085, but 'he succeeded in taking the island from Fingal in 1079' (Godred Crovan, the founder of the dynasty). The page says the kingdom was 'formed c.849', which is outside this batch's Cliopatria shapes. Only the island is page-dated; the Hebrides appear in the 1085 shape.

12,242 km2 for 1085-1093: Mann and the Outer and Inner Hebrides (27 cells, all inside Cliopatria's Viking settlements row and, for 1066-1187, inside its Old Kingdom of Norway shape). The page gives 'total land area of approximately 8,374 square kilometres' (no infobox area), so Cliopatria is 1.46 times larger, within the factor of two; the cells include sea inlets. Godred Crovan held Mann from 1079; the Hebrides are implied by the page (Western Isles troops, Islay), not dated.

correction.text: the 1094 shape without the Irish cells; the southern isles go in 1156 and everything is occupied 1158-1164 (ledger)

keyframe_review.note: 14,607 km2 for 1094-1168, adding 9 Irish cells (the Leinster coast around Dublin and a few cells to the north). The page has Godred Crovan 'also' King of Dublin, undated, 'later ousted from Dublin by Muirchertach Ua Briain', and dying in the plague of 1095; Olave Godredsson was killed in Dublin in 1152. Nothing opened shows the Isles holding Irish land for seventy years, so the Irish cells are taken out of the baseline (a ledger gain and loss at confidence 1 bracket 1094-1095). The southern Inner Hebrides are lost to Somerled's sons in the 1156 division, and Mann and the northern isles are occupied by Somerled 1158-1164 (ledger).

6,003 km2 for 1169-1176: Mann (2 cells), the Outer Hebrides (8) and the northern Inner Hebrides (4 cells in the Highland council area, Skye and its neighbours): exactly the division the page gives after 1156 (Godred keeps Mann, the northern Inner Hebrides and the Outer Hebrides), with Godred back in his territories after Somerled's death in 1164. 0.72 of the page's 8,374 km2. Cliopatria draws it from 1169, five years after Somerled's death and thirteen after the division; the ledger carries the earlier dates.

6,003 km2 for 1177-1259: the same 15 cells as the 1169 shape, renamed Kingdom of Mann in Cliopatria with the same Wikidata id (Q459188) and the same Wikipedia article. The page uses 'Kings of Mann and the Isles' for some later rulers and has the Kings of Mann and the North Isles as 'in theory' Norwegian vassals; the rulers run on unbroken from Godred the Black (to 1187), Raghnall (1187-1228), Olaf the Black (to 1237) and Harald, Ragnvald and Magnus (1237-1265): one state, one dossier.

correction.text: the Cliopatria shape unchanged (Mann, the Outer Hebrides and Skye), for 1260-1266 only

keyframe_review.note: 6,003 km2 for 1260-1271, the same shape. It holds to 1266 only: 'the 1266 Treaty of Perth' yielded the Hebrides and Mann to Scotland; Magnus Olafsson 'was the last of the Norse kings to rule Mann' and Mann was absorbed on his death (1265).

region.text: the Isle of Man, taken from Fingal

ledger.note: 1079: Godred Crovan takes the Isle of Man and founds the Crovan dynasty's Kingdom of Mann and the Isles. 'He succeeded in taking the island from Fingal in 1079', possibly with Western Isles troops (paraphrase); he 'also became King of Dublin' (undated). Cliopatria starts its Isles row in 1085; the page dates the kingdom itself from c.849.

region.text: the Hebrides (Outer and Inner) of Cliopatria's 1085 shape

ledger.note: 1085: the Hebrides join the Isle of Man in Cliopatria's first Kingdom of the Isles shape. The page implies Godred Crovan's rule over the Western Isles (he took Mann possibly with Western Isles troops, and fled to Islay) but dates nothing there; the year is the shape's. The cells are also inside Cliopatria's Viking settlements row.

region.text: Dublin and its surroundings, of which Godred Crovan was king

ledger.note: 1094: Cliopatria extends the Isles to the Irish coast around Dublin. 'He also became King of Dublin' and was 'later ousted from Dublin by Muirchertach Ua Briain': the page dates neither. The year is the shape's.

1095: Godred Crovan dies on Islay and Dublin is gone. He 'fled to Islay, where he died in the plague of 1095'; the page puts his ouster from Dublin by Muirchertach Ua Briain before that, without a year. Dated by his death as the latest possible year.

region.text: the southern Inner Hebrides and Kintyre that Cliopatria drops between its 1094 and 1169 shapes

ledger.note: 1156: after the naval Battle of Epiphany the kingdom is divided and the southern isles go to Somerled's sons. 'The naval Battle of Epiphany in 1156', 'no clear victor'; Godred keeps Mann, the northern Inner Hebrides and the Outer Hebrides, Somerled's sons take the southern Inner Hebrides, Kintyre and the Clyde islands (paraphrase) (Dubgall Mull, Coll, Tiree and Jura; Raghnall Islay and Kintyre; Aonghas Bute). The page's infobox says 'Partitioned: 1164'. Cliopatria drops these cells in 1169.

region.text: Mann, the Outer Hebrides and Skye, Godred's share of 1156

ledger.note: 1158: Somerled invades Mann and Godred flees to Norway. 'Two years later' (after 1156) Somerled invaded Mann and Godred fled to Norway (paraphrase); by about 1158 Somerled was 'undisputed ruler of the entire realm' and declared himself independent of Norway. Drawn hatched: Godred's kingdom is occupied, not annexed.

region.text: Mann, the Outer Hebrides and Skye

ledger.note: 1164: Somerled dies and Godred regains his kingdom. 'Somerled met his death in 1164', possibly assassinated near Renfrew; Godred's brother Ragnald 'reigned for a brief time in 1164' before Godred regained his territories.

1266: the Treaty of Perth gives the Hebrides and Mann to Scotland. 'The 1266 Treaty of Perth' yielded the Hebrides and Mann; Alexander II had begun the Scottish campaign in 1249 ('took personal command of a large fleet'), Haakon died in December 1263 and Magnus Olafsson, 'the last of the Norse kings to rule Mann', died in 1265 (Mann absorbed on his death).

1266: the kingdom ends. Infobox: 'Transferred to Scotland: 1265'; the Treaty of Perth of 1266 completes it. Cliopatria's Kingdom of Mann row runs to 1271 and its Alba shape includes the Isles from 1272.

wars.name: Magnus Barefoot's expeditions
wars.outcome: Norwegian overlordship over the Isles was 're-established by 1098'; in 1098 'Edgar of Scotland signed a treaty with Magnus' on the boundary; the 1102 expedition 'saw incursions into Ireland' and Magnus was 'killed fighting in Ulster' on 23 August 1103.
wars.note: The Norwegian overlordship (the infobox: 'Kingdom under Norwegian suzerainty'; the Kings of Mann and the North Isles 'in theory' vassals) is for the Norway dossier (eu-14) to draw as a vassal tint.

wars.name: Somerled's war on Godred (Battle of Epiphany)

zones.text: the southern Inner Hebrides and Kintyre that Cliopatria drops between its 1094 and 1169 shapes

wars.outcome: After the 'no clear victor' Battle of Epiphany in 1156 the kingdom was divided; two years later Somerled invaded Mann and Godred fled to Norway; Somerled died in 1164 and Godred regained his territories, the southern isles staying with Somerled's sons.

wars.name: Scottish conquest of the Isles
wars.outcome: Alexander II began the Scottish campaign in 1249 and Alexander III continued it; Haakon of Norway died in December 1263 after the Battle of Largs (date not on the page); the 1266 Treaty of Perth yielded the Hebrides and Mann to Scotland.

certainty.note: The island of Mann is a sharp coast; the kingdom's Hebridean extent is approximate and no treaty line fixes it before the 1266 Treaty of Perth, which names the Hebrides and Mann.

sources.title: Kingdom of the Isles
sources.note: Identity, Godred Crovan 1079, the 1156 division, Somerled 1158-1164, the Treaty of Perth 1266; no capital and no infobox area ('total land area of approximately 8,374 square kilometres' in the body).

notes: Pages: 1 of 1-2 budgeted (Kingdom of the Isles). MERGED: Cliopatria's 'Kingdom of the Isles' (1085-1176, 3 shapes) and 'Kingdom of Mann' (1177-1271, 2 shapes) share Wikidata Q459188 and the Wikipedia title, and the Mann shapes are cell-for-cell the 1169 Isles shape: one state, one dossier under the earlier slug with both Names in cliopatria_names. There is no kingdom-of-mann dossier; its colour entry in colours.json is not needed. (1) Start: Cliopatria's row starts in 1085 and the page dates the kingdom from c.849; this dossier starts in 1079 with Godred Crovan taking Mann, the earliest page-dated event with land on the page; the earlier kingdom (c.849-1079, Fingal and the earlier kings) is not in Cliopatria's shapes and not drawn. (2) End: 1266 (Treaty of Perth); the infobox says 1265 and Cliopatria's Mann row runs to 1271. (3) Ireland: Cliopatria adds 9 Irish cells from 1094 and drops them in 1169; the page has Godred Crovan King of Dublin undated, so the cells are bracketed 1094-1095 at confidence 1. (4) Norway: Cliopatria's Old Kingdom of Norway shapes of 1066-1187 contain the 27 Mann and Hebrides cells (all but the 9 Irish ones) and Viking settlements contains all 36 in every year; the page has the Isles under Norwegian suzerainty (re-established by 1098) and Largs/Perth ending it. The Norway dossier (eu-14) should record vassal_start (about 1098) and vassal_end (1266) with the Isles as counterpart; no page opened dates the first accession of Norwegian suzerainty. (5) Somerled's realm (1156-1164 'undisputed ruler of the entire realm' by about 1158; the southern isles to his sons, 'Kings of the Isles' Dubgall and Raghnall) is a state Cliopatria lacks: a dossier for the Kingdom of the Isles/Argyll under Somerled and his sons is for eu-11-x. (6) Rulers omitted: the page's list lacks dates for several reigns (Lagmann 'seven years', Olave 'forty years'). (7) The page says nothing of Alan of Galloway or a numeral for Godred II or Magnus VI; the Battle of Largs has no date there. Failed pages: none.
